smm_pool.text: A restriction period is coming to the US . If you run ads about social issues, elections, or politics, listen up… As Meta has done since 2020 , this restriction period will block any new ads from running during the final week leading up to Election Day. This starts at 12:01 am Pacific Time on October 27th and runs through 11:59 pm on November 3rd. What Restrictions Mean That doesn’t mean that political ads won’t run during this time. But if you want to run political ads between October 27th and November 3rd, they will need to be approved and receive at least one impression before the restriction period starts. Otherwise, you’ll need to wait until the restriction period ends. And if your ads for social issues and politics do run during the restriction period, you’ll be limited on the types of edits you can make. You’ll only be able to make the following edits: Bid Budget Scheduled end date Pause or unpause your ads You won’t be able to make changes to creative, targeting, placement, or optimization. So be prepared. Get Ads Approved Now The worst thing you can do if you run political ads is wait until the last minute. Get these ads approved now so that they can run during the restriction period. smm_pool.text: The good news: Instagram has transparently shared a ton about the magical, majestic Instagram algorithm. The overarching signals — such as watch time, likes, and sends — are the same everywhere. And the principles behind them are evergreen enough to survive the small updates. Follow these, and you’re (mostly) golden. But still, knowing the specifics of how each subset of the algorithm works helps reach your goals faster. Reaching new people on Instagram works a tad differently from deepening relationships with the audience you already have, for instance. Here’s how each algorithm works, the evergreen principles behind all of them, and what to do about it. Key takeaways Instagram has a different algorithm for each part of the app: Instagram ranks feed, stories, explore, and reels separately, using one system for accounts you follow and another for recommendations from accounts you don't. Three signals matter most: Watch time, likes per reach, and sends per reach are the signals Instagram Head Adam Mosseri says carry the most weight in ranking. Likes matter for followers, sends matter more for reaching new people: Likes matter slightly more for reaching your followers, while sends via DM matter slightly more for reaching non-followers. Original content wins: Instagram gives more distribution to the original creator than to reposters, and accounts that mostly repost others' content aren't recommended to non-followers. Viewers can shape what they see: Your Algorithm (in reels and explore), Favorites, and "Not interested" let people tell Instagram what they want more or less of.
